title: Toric Code Anyons, Logical Operators, and Protection

items.title: Periodic square cellulation of the torus
items.statement: For L≥3 let vertices/faces be (Z/LZ)^2 and place one horizontal and one vertical edge at every vertex with periodic incidence; the cellulation has L² vertices, 2L² edges and L² faces.
proof_obligations: Give explicit endpoint/face incidence modulo L and verify each edge has two endpoints and two adjacent faces.

references.title: Alexei Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons
references.locator: §2, printed pp.2–6 (periodic square lattice and toric code)

items.title: Finite square-lattice cycles are boundaries
items.statement: Every finitely supported mod-2 1-cycle in the infinite square lattice, or its dual, is a sum of elementary square boundaries.
proof_obligations: Define finite edge chains on Z² and prove the explicit face-filling formula; verify the same under the dual-grid identification.

items.title: Toric star and plaquette checks
items.statement: Put one qubit on every edge. Define A_v as the product of X over the four incident edges and B_p as the product of Z over the four boundary edges of face p.
proof_obligations: Use the finite tensor-product Pauli definitions and state the check supports explicitly.

items.title: Toric incidence ranks over F₂
items.statement: The primal and dual vertex-edge incidence maps each have rank L²−1 over F₂ because the corresponding graph is connected; their kernels/relations are generated by the constant all-vertex/all-face relation.
proof_obligations: Prove connected incidence rank V−1 by spanning-tree elimination and prove the sole relation is constant on each connected graph. Apply also to the dual graph.

references.title: Alexei Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons

items.title: Toric checks commute and have two global relations
items.statement: All A_v and B_p commute; each star/plaquette pair overlaps on zero or two edges. The products over all vertices and over all faces equal identity.
proof_obligations: Compute Pauli signs from XZ=−ZX and show every edge appears twice in each global product.

items.title: Toric cycle classes are determined by two winding parities
items.statement: Primal and dual torus cycles modulo face and dual-face boundaries have two independent winding parities, represented by the two fundamental loops.
proof_obligations: Give an explicit spanning tree and cycle basis; establish the boundary subspace rank and show the two winding loops complete the basis.

items.title: Toric e and m syndromes
items.statement: A violated A_v check is an e syndrome and a violated B_p check is an m syndrome. Syndrome labels are check eigenvalues −1, not an assumption of a material quasiparticle.
proof_obligations: Define simultaneous syndrome projectors and distinguish the finite stabilizer model from physical particle language.

references.title: Alexei Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons

items.axiom_use: None; this item defines finite syndrome labels.

items.title: Finite toric-code Hamiltonian
items.statement: For J_e,J_m>0 define H=−J_eΣ_v A_v−J_mΣ_p B_p on the finite 2L²-qubit Hilbert space.
proof_obligations: Check H is Hermitian and commuting from the Pauli relations; state energy units and finite volume.

items.title: Toric code encodes two qubits
items.statement: The check rank is 2L²−2, so the common +1 eigenspace in 2L² edge qubits has dimension four and encodes two logical qubits.
proof_obligations: Separate X- and Z-check row spaces; show their ranks add because the Pauli binary symplectic representation has independent X/Z coordinates. Apply the exact stabilizer dimension theorem.

items.title: Open strings create endpoint syndromes
items.statement: A Z product along a primal path anticommutes exactly with the endpoint stars; an X product along a dual path anticommutes exactly with the endpoint plaquettes.
proof_obligations: Count parity of incident path edges at every vertex/face; interior incidences are even and endpoints are odd.

items.title: Toric checks decompose into joint syndrome eigenspaces
items.statement: The toric checks admit a complete orthogonal decomposition into joint eigenspaces; the star and plaquette defect parities are even.
proof_obligations: Use all checks except one fixed star and plaquette as independent generators; construct the sign projectors and prove they are pairwise orthogonal and sum to identity.

items.title: One-crossing e/m strings anticommute
items.statement: A primal Z string and a dual X string crossing once anticommute; their commutator phase is −1. This is the exact mutual e/m string-algebra sign.
proof_obligations: Use the Pauli relation on the unique shared edge; distinguish the algebraic sign from a dynamical braiding experiment.

items.title: Noncontractible toric logical loops
items.statement: A primal Z or dual X loop around either noncontractible torus cycle commutes with every stabilizer and acts as a logical Pauli operator on the four-dimensional code.
proof_obligations: State cycle homology classes in H₁(T²;F₂) and dual classes; define the four logical representatives.

items.title: Exact finite-volume toric gap
items.statement: The ground space is the four-dimensional toric code and the spectral gap is 4 min(J_e,J_m): global parity requires at least two violations of either type, and an open string realizes a cheapest pair.
proof_obligations: Diagonalize all commuting checks; use the two global relations to require even e and m defect parity; compute each violation cost 2J_a and construct an endpoint pair for the smaller coupling.

references.title: Alexei Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons

items.title: Exact indistinguishability in a contractible disk
items.statement: For a cellulated contractible disk D, every operator O supported in D compresses to a scalar on the code: ΠOΠ=c(O)Π.
proof_obligations: Expand O in the finite Pauli basis. A Pauli anticommuting with a check compresses to zero; a Pauli commuting with all checks gives primal and dual cycles in D, which bound 2-chains and hence are stabilizers up to phase. Extend by linearity. State the disk/cellulation hypothesis exactly.

items.title: Two anticommuting toric logical Pauli pairs
items.statement: The two independent primal/dual homology directions give two logical X/Z pairs with the Pauli commutation matrix and identity cross-pairings.
proof_obligations: Use mod-2 intersection number on the torus and show distinct parallel cycles have zero intersection while dual cycles intersect once.

items.title: Toric code distance is L
items.statement: The minimum weight of a nontrivial logical Pauli is L: every noncontractible primal/dual loop has at least L edges and a straight fundamental loop attains L.
proof_obligations: Prove the lower bound by projecting a nontrivial cycle to a nonzero winding in at least one periodic coordinate; prove upper bound with a straight loop. Contractible cycles are stabilizers.

references.title: Alexei Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons

items.title: Pauli-path energy barrier
items.statement: For a logical Pauli L, its barrier is the minimum, over local-Pauli paths from I to L, of the maximum intermediate energy above the ground energy.
proof_obligations: Define path locality, order of single-edge errors and max-minus-ground energy; keep this finite code quantity distinct from thermal lifetime.

items.title: Toric code corrects fewer than L/2 arbitrary Pauli errors
items.statement: For an error-correction radius t with 2t<L, the root stabilizer distance theorem gives exact correction of all Pauli errors of weight at most t.
proof_obligations: Check strict integer-distance inequality and carry the theorem’s Pauli/stabilizer hypotheses without asserting an unproved noisy-hardware procedure.

items.title: Toric logical string has constant energy barrier
items.statement: A noncontractible logical string of the cheaper species can be grown edge by edge with at most two endpoint defects; its barrier is at most 4 min(J_e,J_m), independent of L.
proof_obligations: Give the explicit sequential path and compute energy after each step. Do not infer a finite-temperature lifetime, self-correction or perturbative stability.

items.title: A finite gap does not prove a stable material phase
items.statement: The exact finite commuting Hamiltonian gap and disk indistinguishability are mathematical finite-volume statements; neither alone proves physical topological-phase existence, perturbation stability, or a positive-temperature memory lifetime.
proof_obligations: Separate exact finite-model theorems from thermodynamic-limit and empirical claims; cite no stability/open-phase theorem as a premise.

proof_obligations: Verify every check commutation by support overlap and calculate the gap for J_e,J_m.

items.title: Planar and periodic surface-code distances differ
items.statement: The existing square planar surface-code theorem has boundary-dependent asymmetric distances; it is not the periodic toric lattice and cannot supply torus homology counts.
proof_obligations: Compare the actual boundary conventions, logical path classes, and distance statements; preserve the rough/dual asymmetry.
